notes: Approved-food lists for the two elimination diets the app plans for. In strict mode (the default when a plan restricts one of these families) a recipe is safe only when every ingredient is on the list or on the person's own tolerated list.

Low FODMAP: foods that the Monash-group composition papers and the Halmos 2014 trial diet list as low FODMAP at a usual serve. Where a serving threshold is published only in the Monash app it is not reproduced here; the portion field then says 'usual serve' and the item note says so. Foods whose safe serve is small are marked 'small serve' with the published basis.

Low histamine: foods that the SIGHI compatibility list rates as well tolerated (0), as encoded in this app's dictionary from the SIGHI list and Comas-Baste 2020. The SIGHI leaflet could not be machine-read in this build, so items whose rating was not re-checked against the leaflet carry verified: false and a note. Freshness matters more than the list: fresh or quickly frozen, cooked and eaten the same day.
Every item carries sources. A person can add foods they tolerate and remove foods they react to; those live on the person, never in this file.

low-fodmap.label: low FODMAP
low-fodmap.intro: Foods that are low FODMAP at a usual serve during the elimination phase. Amounts matter: a few items are safe only in a small serve, and stacking several 'small serve' foods in one meal adds up. Portion thresholds published only in the Monash app are not reproduced here.

stacking.text: Amounts matter: a few items are safe only in a small serve, and stacking several 'small serve' foods in one meal adds up.
stacking.note: 2026-09 audit. Recipes and labels show the portion for each food this list allows only in a limited amount, and a meal with two or more foods marked 'small serve' is a caution. Set amounts such as 'ten nuts' or 'half a cup dry' show a note but do not count (owner question 7, answered September 30, 2026): they are ordinary serving sizes at which the food is low FODMAP, and the Monash team sets those cut-offs conservatively so foods can be combined in a meal, while 'small serve' foods are fine only below an ordinary serve. Varney 2017: cut-offs were set from the FODMAP content of typical serving sizes. Shepherd 2008: symptoms came on in a dose-dependent manner, with fructose and fructans alone or combined. See docs/VERIFY-log.md.

low-histamine.label: low histamine
low-histamine.intro: Foods the SIGHI leaflet rates as well tolerated, for a short elimination trial. Freshness matters as much as the food: fresh or quickly frozen, cooked and eaten the same day, no leftovers, no stocks except a quick homemade vegetable stock. Foods the leaflet rates as risky are left out during the trial. Every item was checked against the leaflet (version 2021-11-17) except the few marked 'not re-checked' (seeds, cinnamon, and nutmeg), which it does not rate. Later, what you tolerate matters more than any list: add foods you tolerate under your own list.

basis_legend.measured histamine: Lab measurements of the food explain its place: histamine found in foods to leave out, none or little in foods on the list (Sánchez-Pérez 2021: foods sold in Spain, Table 1).
basis_legend.other amines: No histamine was found, but other amines were, mainly putrescine, which may slow the breakdown of histamine in the gut. Sánchez-Pérez 2021 calls the evidence for that scarce.
basis_legend.proposed liberator: Said to make the body release its own histamine. Sánchez-Pérez 2021: the mechanism has not been shown, and no clinical studies in humans support it.
basis_legend.SIGHI rating only: No measurement in the cited sources; the rating rests on the SIGHI list and leaflet (a patient organization, from experience reports and the literature).

stacking.text: Amounts matter: tolerance depends on how much you eat, so a few items are listed for a limited amount.
stacking.note: Owner question 7, September 30, 2026: recipes and labels show the portion for each low histamine item listed for a limited amount. There is no stacking caution: the leaflet gives no count. SIGHI leaflet, page 1: "The compatibility is highly dependent on the individual sensitivity and the amount consumed."
